title: Allocation-failure paths leak across engine/definition; no checkAllAllocationFailures coverage
scope: Root cause of the memory-leak signature recurring across 18 distinct pipeline runs (2026-05-28 -> 2026-08-05).
symptom: DebugAllocator reports leaks during integration runs. Named sites: transition.zig cloneJsonValueSafe/processNodeEntry (TC-EE-10-06), transition.zig parseTimerConfig (31 leaks), definition/store.zig parseGraphJson (GH #406, closed 08-03, recurred).
reproduction: Non-deterministic by nature: an error path leaks only when a run happens to trigger it. zig build test-engine passes clean because unit tests exercise happy paths only.
root_cause_analysis: Leaks are on allocation-failure/error paths that no test exercises. transition.zig has 51 allocation sites but only 12 errdefer guards. std.testing.checkAllAllocationFailures and FailingAllocator are used nowhere in the repo, so no error path is systematically exercised. Each of the 18 runs patched the one site it hit; none added the coverage that would find the class.
acceptance_criteria: checkAllAllocationFailures tests exist for cloneJsonValueSafe/cloneObjectMapSafe, parseTimerConfig, parseGraphJson
Those tests fail against pre-fix main and pass after the fix
zig build test exits 0 with no DebugAllocator leak output
Tests wired into zig build test so coverage cannot lapse
evidence_file: Audit corpus: 18 runs with leak FAILs, most recent WF03-gh419-20260805
root_cause_correction: The '51 allocation sites / 12 errdefer guards' figure in root_cause_analysis is OUTDATED and UNDERSTATED. Measured 2026-08-07: transition.zig's production region (lines 1-2166, excluding its 29 in-file test blocks) holds 110 allocation sites against 15 errdefer guards; the whole file has 170 alloc sites. src/definition/store.zig holds 35 alloc sites against 8 errdefer guards and, critically, ZERO test blocks. The direction of the analysis is unchanged and reinforced: errdefer coverage is sparser relative to allocation density than reported.
resolution: Two-part remedy. (1) Prior run GH #428 (commit 55f7768) had already landed TC-ISS-0132-01/02 (parseTimerConfig) and TC-ISS-0132-03 (cloneJsonValueSafe/cloneObjectMapSafe) via std.testing.checkAllAllocationFailures, together with their fixes (errdefer on repeat_expression; OutOfMemory no longer collapsed into InvalidTimerConfig; errdefer guards in the clone helpers) and the src/transition_test_root.zig refAllDecls shim wiring them into zig build test. (2) This run closed the remaining gap: parseGraphJson in src/definition/store.zig, which had no coverage of any kind because store.zig contained zero test blocks and was reachable from no addTest root. Added TC-ISS-0132-04/05, proved they reproduce the leaks against main's unmodified parseGraphJson ('1 pass, 2 fail (3 total); 2 leaks' — TC-04 fail_index 6/25, allocated 1713 / freed 1711, at store.zig:1344 (.label dupe); TC-05 fail_index 9/11, allocated 1807 / freed 1805, at store.zig:1366 (.source dupe)), then fixed three defects: PGJ-1 a fragile errdefer-plus-bare-deinit pairing replaced by a single defer; PGJ-2 and PGJ-3 partial-struct-construction leaks in the nodes and edges loops, where a struct literal ran 3 (resp. 5) fallible dupes before the row's *_built counter was incremented, so a failure on a later field left every earlier dupe of that row unowned and unfreed. Fixed by duping each field into a local guarded by its own errdefer before assembling the struct. Added src/definition_store_test_root.zig and wired run_definition_store_tests into the aggregate test_step.
prevention: checkAllAllocationFailures is now established in the repo with an explanatory header block in both src/engine/transition.zig and src/definition/store.zig instructing that any function allocating more than once before returning be added to the harness. Wiring is enforced mechanically: tools/lint_test_wiring.py runs inside zig build test and FAILED this run when the new Run artifact was attached only to its narrow test-definition-store step — attaching it to the aggregate test_step was required to make it pass. That linter is what prevents this coverage from silently lapsing, which is the exact failure mode (inert tests, ISS-0102 / ISS-0150 class) that let the leak class survive 18 runs.
